## Overview

The She people (畲族) are an ethnic group native to southern China and one of the 56 ethnic groups officially recognized by the People’s Republic of China. According to the 2021 China Statistical Yearbook, their total population was 746,385, including 403,516 males and 342,869 females. They are the largest ethnic minority in Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi provinces and are also present in Anhui and Guangdong. The She include speakers of Shanke dialect, an unclassified Chinese variety heavily influenced by Hakka Chinese, and approximately 1,200 people in Guangdong who speak She, a critically endangered Hmong–Mien language. The roughly 45,000 She living in Guizhou form a separate subgroup called the Dongjia.

## Foodways

The sources describe historical She subsistence and salt production. After migration into hilly areas of Jiangxi and Fujian, the She became hillside farmers whose methods included burning grasses on slopes, casting rice seeds onto the embers, and harvesting the produce after the growth season. Some She also participated in producing and trading salt obtained through evaporation of local pools of salt water.

## Language & religion

The She people use several distinct linguistic varieties. Over 400,000 She people in Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi speak Shanke dialect (山客话; Shānkèhuà), an unclassified Chinese variety heavily influenced by Hakka Chinese. Approximately 1,200 She people in Guangdong speak She (畲语; Shēyǔ), also called Ho Ne, a critically endangered Hmong–Mien language. She has two main dialects: Luofu, the Western She dialect, and Lianhua, the Eastern She dialect.
